subject: Re: StoreTech private offer — commit vs list-price realignment
messages:
From: Paul Henderson <phenderson@storatech.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure marketplace packaging — clarification and ask

Ben —

Thanks for the call earlier. A couple of things procurement asked me to follow up on so we can move the AWS/GCP/Azure private offer conversation to approval:

- The private offer price on Azure is attractive, but the way the commitment maps to the list-price tiers makes our channel partner margin math messy. Can you confirm whether the committed SKU set can be listed at a single consolidated list price while we take a lower private-offer net?
- We need a simple example showing how a $1.2M 12‑month commit would be invoiced through Azure Marketplace and how much the distributor/reseller receives (percent passback).

Also attaching the SOW so you can confirm billing milestones.

Paul
Director of Cloud Procurement
StoreTech

Attachments: StoreTech_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Henderson <phenderson@storatech.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace packaging — clarification and ask

Paul —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and I've attached an SKU mapping worksheet.

- Yes, we can publish a consolidated list-price for the committed SKU family. The private-offer net can be set as an off-market discount applied at purchase time; that allows channels to invoice off the consolidated list and receive agreed passback.
- Example invoice flow attached (see tab ‘Example-1’). For a $1.2M 12mo commit we typically model a 20–28% distributor/reseller passback depending on whether the partner is acting as reseller versus referral (I included both scenarios).

Next step — can we set a 30‑minute call Tuesday to review the invoice example and the channel passback table? Naomi and Jordan will join to lock in the passback and listing approach.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: azure-sku-mapping.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: StoreTech passback math and options

Ben/Jordan —

Quick internal note before the Tuesday call: I ran three passback scenarios and documented in the workbook Ben attached. High-level options we should be ready to propose to StoreTech:

1) Consolidated list price + fixed % passback (transparent, easiest for procurement) — reseller gets 24% flat, distributor gets 6% (30% total).
2) Tiered passback linked to consumption buckets — start at 20% and step to 30% if commit usage thresholds met (protects margins early).
3) Gross-to-net with escrow for overage credits — lowers listed commitment but requires monthly reconciliation (higher ops overhead).

Notes for the call:
- If StoreTech wants a single list price, we should avoid >35% total passback to preserve unit economics.
- For Azure private offers, we can structure the private-offer net as a DocuSign-backed amendment (DocuSign link in hubspot).

I’ll bring a one-page comparison and the invoice example. Jordan — please prepare a short slide showing how reseller invoicing vs distributor reseller-invoice flow differs (they asked explicitly).

Naomi
Head of Partner Pricing | Redwood Inference

From: procurement@storatech.com <procurement@storatech.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Paul Henderson <phenderson@storatech.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Partner Manager <am-partner@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace packaging — clarification and ask

Ben/Team —

Appreciate the quick responses. A few procurement constraints to flag before the call:

- Our CFO will only sign if the distributor net does not exceed 26% of list for the first 6 months. After that we can entertain step-ups tied to usage.
- We need billing to flow through the Marketplace for auditability; any off-market adjustments must be visible in the invoice reconciliation.
- Can Redwood provide a single-line example invoice and a short note on tax handling for Azure Marketplace transactions?

We uploaded a slightly revised SOW to the DocuSign envelope — please confirm you can accept the milestone schedule linked below.

Thanks,
StoreTech Procurement Team

Related link: https://app.docusign.com/StoreTech-PO-2027

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Henderson <phenderson@storatech.com>, procurement@storatech.com
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Partner Manager <am-partner@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Sep 2027 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace packaging — clarification and ask

Paul / Procurement —

Thanks for the constraints — helpful and reasonable. Action items from our side before Tuesday: 

- Naomi will finalize passback option 1 (consolidated list + fixed passback at 24% reseller / 6% distributor) and produce a single-line example invoice that shows list, marketplace transaction, private-offer adjustment, and passback.
- Jordan will create a one-slide flow for reseller vs distributor invoice routing and highlight where tax sits in each flow.
- I will confirm that the DocuSign amendment can attach to the private offer and share the DocuSign view link.

We’ll aim to keep the initial distributor net at 30% total but will cap to 26% for the first 6 months per your CFO request and outline a usage-stepped uplift thereafter. If that sounds acceptable I’ll send a proposed amendment this afternoon for you to review.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Tuesday 09/12 10:00am PT. Is that good for you?

Best,
Ben

Attachments referenced in thread: azure-sku-mapping.xlsx, StoreTech_SOW_v2.pdf
